_notes: Every value here is null. The estimated values are WITHHELD: they are the result of the private project,
not its method. The structure is what the code needs; fill it in from your own estimation.
Any null makes a loader refuse to run, as sim_config.template.json already does in this project.
Units: spreads and spread states in basis points; shock variances q in bp^2 per business day; rate-model
quantities in decimal per year; lattice factor variances in decimal^2 per business day.

four_state._shape: 37 parameters, in the order of fourstate4.NAMES
four_state._rating_curve: G_t(n) = a + b (n - n0) + c (n - n0)^2, each coefficient an AR(1) with its own mean
four_state._bond_own_part: B: AR(1), mean 0, starts at 0 on the bond's first trading day
four_state._permanent_level: u: no shock; prior variance s2_u, prior mean from the new-issue regression
four_state._liquidity: L: AR(1), mean 0, with three daily measures x_k = al_k + be_k L + e_k, Var(e_k) = h_k
four_state._dealer_inventory: D: AR(1) driven by customer order flow; lam_D maps it into the spread
four_state._trade_level: bias b_j = g1 + g2 lv (customer buy), g3 + g4 lv (customer sell), 0 otherwise; log R_j = d0 + d1 lv + d2 cust
four_state._issue_observation: the issue spread observed once, on the bond's first trading day: iss = s + iss_d + e, Var(e) = iss_v
four_state._issuer_factor: C_k: AR(1) shared by the issuer's bonds, with a per-bond loading beta

design_constants._notes: Not estimated, but chosen before any result; the values in force are withheld.
design_constants._n0: the rating notch the curve is centred on, on the Moody's scale (Aaa = 1 ... C = 21)
design_constants._lv: mean and s.d. of log par volume used to standardise lv, fixed from the first estimation window
design_constants._window: length of the rolling estimation window; re-estimated at each month end

rate_model._shape: 20 parameters, in the order of afns.NAMES: a shadow-rate arbitrage-free Nelson-Siegel model

_notes: The lattice does not estimate these: the rate factor is fitted to the rate model's term variances
(tree2.fit_ar1 on tree2.afns_short_rate_var) and the credit factor to the four-state model's credit
variance (tree2.credit_var). rho and the call-intensity coefficients are estimated.
The inversion tree and the prediction tree must use the SAME values -- see oas_obs.py.
lattice._step: business days per lattice step; a numerical setting chosen by a convergence check

recovery._notes: recovery of face value by payment-rank group (recovery.GROUPS), per estimation window
recovery._numerics: h_step is the integration step in years and lam_max the search bound; numerical settings
